stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on July 17th.
stocks.news:
Stocks slid into the weekend. The NASDAQ led the way down, off 1.40% to 25,520, the S&P 500 gave back 1.01% to 7,457, and the DOW eased 0.77% to 52,146.

Two names did the talking. Meta fell 2.97% even as reports surfaced that Anthropic is exploring renting roughly $10 billion of Meta's computing power, a reminder that the AI buildout is now big enough that rivals rent from each other. Lucid jumped 13.93% after flatly denying a report that it was preparing to file for bankruptcy, calling it "completely false." That leaves the EV maker up more than 30% over five sessions and still down more than 30% for the year, which tells you how much ground there was to make up.

economy.note: The 10-Year, Brent, stocks, and crypto are as of the July 17th close; gold and silver are live spot quotes taken Monday morning, July 20th.
economy.commentary:
The 10-Year Treasury barely moved at 4.55%. The commodity desk more than made up for it.

Brent crude jumped 2.58% to $90.37, its first close above $90 since June 11, after strikes tied to the Iran and U.S. conflict raised fears of a supply disruption at the tankers (chart below). Zoom out and this is the second act, not the first: Brent spiked to $138.21 on April 7 before falling all the way back to the high $60s in early July. From that July 2 low of $68.53, oil has run up nearly 32% in about two weeks.

The metals split, which does not happen often. Gold slipped 0.40% to about $4,001 and is drifting toward nine month lows, while silver pushed 1.55% higher to $56.77.

Why a REALTOR® cares about a barrel of oil: higher crude usually shows up at the pump within a couple of weeks, and gas is one of the few prices households feel every single week. It also feeds the inflation read the Fed is watching, which is the same read that sets mortgage rates.

feature_image.caption: Brent closed at $90.37, its first finish above $90 since June 11, and up nearly 32% from the July 2 low of $68.53. April's $138.21 spike shows how fast this market can move in both directions.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET, July 17th.
crypto.commentary:
Crypto basically held its breath. Bitcoin added 0.05% to $64,721, Ether ticked up 0.04% to $1,871, and XRP eased 0.27% to $1.10.

The news was less quiet. A Florida student drained at least $220,000 from about 80 wallets by dressing up malware as free video games on Steam, and crypto real estate firm RealT is winding down and selling all 700 of its Detroit properties after raising roughly $140 million to let investors buy fractional stakes in rentals. Chainalysis estimates crypto scams take $14 billion to $17 billion a year. The lesson travels well beyond crypto: if the returns are effortless and the paperwork is thin, slow down.

real_estate.homebuilder: Affordability Tightens For A Fifth Straight Month As The June Existing Home Median Hits $446,400; The Longer Arc Says Rates Did The Damage, Not Prices
real_estate.commentary:
The daily 30-year fixed eased to 6.63% and the 15-year to 6.16%, both a touch friendlier than Thursday.

That help arrived late. Buying a home got harder for the fifth month in a row, and the National Association of REALTORS® put the June median for existing homes at $446,400. Most American households now need a six figure income to carry a typical home, which is why so many buyers are parked on the sidelines waiting for either prices or rates to blink.

Zoom out and the price story is calmer than the affordability story. On the Census and HUD quarterly measure, the national median sale price is $403,200, roughly 8.9% below its late 2022 peak of $442,600 (chart below). Read those two numbers together and the point lands: prices drifted sideways to lower for three years. Rates did the damage. That also means the day financing gets cheaper, the sidelined demand does not have far to climb back.

Housing is turning political, too. Young voters now rank home affordability as their top concern ahead of the midterms, above food prices, and 49% of renters are paying more than 30% of income on rent.

📍 Local Snapshot (Live MLS Inventory)

• Buyable right now: 733 listings across the five cities we track, refreshed this morning.
• Fremont: 285 listings, with 209 active, 37 new this week, and 38 coming soon.
• Hayward: 204. Milpitas: 106. Newark: 82. Union City: 56.
• In the pipeline: 91 coming soon across the five cities, which is next week's supply already lining up, plus 68 brand new this week.
• Board wide: 2,788 listings across the 15 city table above, down 35 from Thursday.

Supply is easing back while rates tick down. That combination usually firms up the entry level first, so if you have been waiting for a softer Fremont, the window is not getting wider.

feature_image.caption: The national median sale price is $403,200, about 8.9% below its late 2022 peak of $442,600. Prices drifted sideways to lower for three years while affordability still got worse, which tells you rates did the damage.
feature_image.source: Source: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, via FRED (MSPUS). Quarterly, not seasonally adjusted.
